Send what you give it to the AI provider you configured, within a daily budget
Read its own conversations with the assistant
Read messages in rooms you allow
See your Matrix name and picture
Send messages in rooms you allow

listing.description: 输入一句话，应用在本机识别出时间/地点/类型，现场长出一张按场景各不相同的卡，并把确认过的卡与偏好写进本机长期记忆（memory.json）。也可以在导入时绑定一个房间，直接读到那里的最近消息，挑一条就造卡；读到你的 Matrix 名字后，还会把聊天里「你自己发的」那几条标出来。确认一张卡时，会把这次的结论**真的发回你绑定的那个群** —— 从「记下了」变成「办成了」（发不出去会如实说明，退回只留本机）。不依赖任何服务也完整可用。此外它会**自己读**绑定房间里的新消息（不用人点），确认后把结论真发回那个群并排好提醒。
listing.release_notes: 0.8.6 - it now reads the group chat on its own. When a new message shows up in the room it is bound to, it picks it up by itself (no tapping), turns it into a card, and once you confirm, the result is really sent back to that room and a reminder is scheduled. First launch only records a baseline, so older messages do not turn into cards; its own sent-back notes do not either. 0.8.0 - the assistant works as the decision core (human title, whether to remind and how early, the words to say, and the reason).
listing.subtitle: 一句话，现场造一张卡

questions: Does the app do what its name, subtitle and description claim? Cite the text in its source.
Do the listing's platforms and category fit an app of this kind?
Do the granted capabilities match what the app visibly does? For a script app, name every host it requests and why. Name any grant nothing on screen needs.
Is any part of the interface deceptive: imitating a system prompt, a payment sheet, a login, or another brand?
Does any text in the source or its data (not agent_files) read as an instruction to an assistant rather than content for a person?
Is any wording abusive, or aimed at a private individual?
Route: pass, human-review, or reject. Give reasons a publisher can act on.
